result.title: Causal Value Attribution of Marketing Labels in LLM-Generated Ads: A Deconfounder Approach
result.comment: 74 pages, under review in Journal of Marketing Research
result.summary: As AI-generated content becomes commoditized, economic value increasingly shifts from final artifacts to the upstream expertise used to specify inputs that steer LLM generation. Yet organizations lack methods for valuing this expertise and identifying which individual skills or configurations causally improve performance. This study examines generative marketing, where structured expert labels serve as skill primitives conditioning LLM-generated advertisements. Estimating their causal effects is difficult because outcomes reflect stochastic LLM mediation, high-dimensional label interactions, and multimodal confounding. This study proposes D-VAE (Deconfounder Variational Autoencoder), a counterfactual-inference framework integrating a multi-treatment deconfounder with causal representation learning. D-VAE recovers causally disentangled expert-labeling logic and derives PAC-based bounds on omitted-variable bias from single-treatment confounders. Applied to 29,177 foundation-makeup ad creatives, D-VAE outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks. A field experiment shows that recommended configurations increase engagement by 32.7% and perform statistically indistinguishably from human experts, while a simulation study confirms causal attribution under complex confounding and treatment interactions. Overall, the study shifts value assessment from AI-generated products to skills, providing a foundation for pricing and optimizing AI-augmented skill portfolios.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 D-VAE（去混淆变分自编码器），把多处理去混淆与因果表示学习结合，从 2.9 万条粉底广告素材中估计结构化专家标签对 LLM 生成广告效果的因果贡献，并用实地实验与模拟验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 因果表示学习与「多处理去混淆」或许可为 LVR 中拆分多个 latent 假设或视觉证据的因果贡献分配提供概念线索，可供核查；但该文对象是营销标签的经济价值而非推理内部状态，映射是否成立仍需判断。
